card.name: Mid-sentence words in old encyclopedic prose
card.fires_on: Ordinary words in the middle of a sentence in old encyclopedia or essay-style text on history, science or philosophy. These include names, articles, verbs and adjectives.

modes.label: Historical names and topics
modes.description: A proper name or noun in a history question or biography sentence.
modes.example: Why is the battle of<< Marathon>> counted among the decisive battles of the world

modes.label: Small connecting words
modes.description: A short word such as as, a, some, there or he that leads into the next noun phrase.
modes.example: The druids had<< a>> pontifex maximus, to whom

modes.label: Descriptive verbs and adjectives
modes.description: A verb or adjective that comes before the key noun of a descriptive claim.
modes.example: Memnon, who possessed great<< military>> skill and experience, succeeded him in his
